findings.statement: The original DOCX expressly permits definitions and appropriate simplifications. The nine primary requirements retain the geometric definition, separate event calendars, astronomical-reference check, Beijing dates and all six other cities. Apparent geocentric equatorial forcing, GAST rotation and WGS84 observer subtraction form an adequate conditional coordinate model for the stated airless, nominal-site scenario. No omitted primary question or demonstrated numerical contradiction was found within that conditional scope.

findings.target: Validation independence, narrow windows and event completeness
findings.statement: Producer and checker use distinct interpolation/parallax/root implementations, but share JPL dynamics, approximate sidereal theory and the same interval-pairing logic. The existing checker reconstructs all dates and counts; native audit inspected the search domains and verified reported endpoints rather than launching another full event search. No missed event counterexample was found, but this is not an independent continuous ephemeris-accuracy certificate. The narrowest nominal window, Kunming 2016-07-20, lasts 15.936344861984253 seconds. Its lunar and solar slopes are approximately 0.0033971873 and -0.0032893388 degrees/second; the 0.05-degree reference acceptance tolerance corresponds to about 14.72 and 15.20 seconds respectively. The two-second algorithm-agreement tolerance therefore cannot guarantee physical existence or timing of every narrow window. Current conditional and visibility limitations are necessary and must accompany these outputs.
findings.required_test: Compare the frozen narrow-window duration and endpoint altitude slopes with the distinct angular and timing tolerances; inspect full-date enumeration and source dependence.
findings.pass_condition: Retain conditional numerical scope and explicitly distinguish implementation agreement, sampled reference accuracy and real observing-window robustness.
